cards.explanation: The answer is True. Moses says, “The fruit of your womb will be cursed, as well as the produce of your land, the calves of your herds, and the lambs of your flocks.” (Deuteronomy 28:18). Family, fields and flocks are all named in that verse. Just before it, he says they will be cursed in the city and cursed in the country (Deuteronomy 28:16).

The answer is everything they put their hand to, friends. The LORD will send “…confusion and reproof in all to which you put your hand…” (Deuteronomy 28:20). Moses doesn't narrow that to one kind of work. He says it lasts until they are destroyed and quickly perish because of the wickedness they have committed in forsaking Him.

The word is forsaking, bakers. Moses says the curses come because of “…the wickedness you have committed in forsaking Him.” (Deuteronomy 28:20). Forsaking means walking away from the LORD. Moses names that as the reason.

The answer is dust and powder. Moses says the LORD will turn the rain of their land “…into dust and powder…” (Deuteronomy 28:24). I know a little about dust, friends, since I sat under years of it in a junk drawer. Rain that comes down as powder is no kind of rain.

The answer is False. It's Israel who does the fleeing, friends. Moses says, “You will march out against them in one direction but flee from them in seven.” (Deuteronomy 28:25). They go out one way and run seven ways. In that verse, the LORD is the one who causes them to be defeated before their enemies.

The answer is an object of horror. Moses says, “You will be an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.” (Deuteronomy 28:25). That's what defeat looks like to everyone watching. It's a heavy line.

The answer is False, friends. Moses says they will be oppressed and plundered day after day, “…with no one to save you.” (Deuteronomy 28:29). Nobody comes to the rescue in that picture. It's a heavy moment, and I'll leave it at that.

The answer is that he will not live in it. Moses says, “You will build a house but will not live in it.” (Deuteronomy 28:30). All that work goes in and he never lives there. Picture painting every wall and never getting to hang your coat by the door.

The answer is False, bakers. Moses says, “You will plant a vineyard but will not enjoy its fruit.” (Deuteronomy 28:30). The planting happens and the enjoying doesn't. It's the same kind of loss as the house right before it.

The answer is True. Moses says their sons and daughters will be given to another nation, “…while your eyes grow weary looking for them day after day…” (Deuteronomy 28:32). I think this one hurts, friends. Moses also says they will have no power in their hand.

The answer is gods of wood and stone. Moses says they will worship other gods, “…gods of wood and stone.” (Deuteronomy 28:36). Wood and stone, friends! I've stamped plenty of dough in my day, and not one lump ever answered me back. That's the picture Moses paints, and it's a sad one: the LORD's people bowing to gods that can't hear a word.

The word is locusts, bakers. Moses says, “You will sow much seed in the field but harvest little, because the locusts will consume it.” (Deuteronomy 28:38). Much seed goes in and little comes out. That's a lot of work for a very small payoff.

The answer is that the foreigner will rise higher and become the head. Moses says, “The foreigner living among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink down lower and lower.” (Deuteronomy 28:43). He adds, “He will be the head, and you will be the tail.” (Deuteronomy 28:44). The positions flip, friends.

The answer is that they did not serve the LORD with joy and gladness. Moses says, “Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart in all your abundance…” (Deuteronomy 28:47). He ties it to abundance, friends. They had plenty and didn't serve with joy and gladness of heart.

The word is enemies, bakers. Moses says, “…you will serve your enemies the LORD will send against you in famine, thirst, nakedness, and destitution.” (Deuteronomy 28:48). He adds that the LORD will place an iron yoke on their neck. It's a heavy picture of a hard road.

The answer is False, friends. Moses describes “…a nation whose language you will not understand…” (Deuteronomy 28:49). Somebody is shouting at you, and you can't catch a single word. You'd just nod and smile like I do when a recipe is written in tiny letters. He says this nation comes from afar and swoops down like an eagle.

The answer is no respect for the old and no pity for the young. Moses calls it “…a ruthless nation with no respect for the old and no pity for the young.” (Deuteronomy 28:50). The old get no respect from it and the young get no pity. Ruthless is the word Moses picks, friends.

The answer is the high fortified walls they trust in. Moses says they will besiege the cities “…until the high and fortified walls in which you trust have fallen.” (Deuteronomy 28:52). The walls are what they trust in, and they come down. It's a hard picture, bakers.

The answer is True, friends. Moses says even “The most gentle and refined man among you…” will begrudge his brother, his wife and his surviving children (Deuteronomy 28:54). He has nothing left in the siege (Deuteronomy 28:55). I think this is one of the hardest parts of the whole passage.

The answer is True. Moses says, “He will afflict you again with all the diseases you dreaded in Egypt, and they will cling to you.” (Deuteronomy 28:60). The diseases they dreaded come back. That's one of the warnings he gives, bakers.

The answer is False, friends. Moses says the LORD will also bring “…every sickness and plague not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed.” (Deuteronomy 28:61). The list in the book isn't the end of it. That's a sobering line.

The word is few. Moses says, “You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left few in number, because you would not obey the voice of the LORD your God.” (Deuteronomy 28:62). From stars to few, bakers. That's quite a drop.

The answer is among all the nations, friends. Moses says, “Then the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other…” (Deuteronomy 28:64). That comes after he says they will be uprooted from the land they are entering to possess (Deuteronomy 28:63). He adds that there they will worship other gods, gods of wood and stone.

The word is dread. Moses says they will say those words “…because of the dread in your hearts of the terrifying sights you will see.” (Deuteronomy 28:67). I think that means no hour feels safe to them, friends. That's a hard way to live.

The answer is that no one will buy them. Moses says, “There you will sell yourselves to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.” (Deuteronomy 28:68). They offer themselves and nobody takes the offer. I think that's about as low as it gets, friends, and it closes out Moses' list of curses.
